Subject: BrightPixel — proposed capacity ramp + SOW edits

Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As flagged on the call we are planning a Q4 feature ramp and want to secure additional capacity sooner. Attached is a short Order Form with updated throughput tiers and an edited SOW (v3) that reflects the expanded implementation work (data connectors + prefix caching configuration).

Top asks:
- Add 2x reserved capacity pool starting 2025-09-01 (estimated spike through Dec).
- Adjust monthly fee schedule to reflect blended rate for committed capacity + burst.
- Add an implementation milestone for connector work with acceptance criteria.

Can your team review and confirm if these changes are acceptable from both commercial and security perspectives? We need a signed order by 2025-08-10 to hit our procurement window.

I attached a one-page redline of the SOW to make edits easier.

Thanks,
Sasha

- Fees: the blended monthly fee in the spreadsheet looks reasonable; need Finance to confirm ramp credits and proration model.
- SOW changes: the connector milestones look fine but the acceptance criteria are loose. Please tighten definitions for "connector pass" and "performance baseline" so our ops team can validate.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Legal to propose redline for Order Form and MSA references (exhibit, effective date, billing cycle).
2) Product/Oncall to confirm connector acceptance tests (I'll loop in CS if needed).
3) I will provide the DocuSign link and implementation timeline once legal confirms language.

—Vanessa

Team — I reviewed the SOW redline and the Order Form. High-level: we can accept the commercial structure but need the following legal edits before countersignature. I've attached an annotated Order Form and an excerpted MSA clause suggestions.

Required contract edits (summary):
1) Exhibit reference: ensure Order Form explicitly references MSA v2.1 (effective date 2024-11-01) to avoid ambiguity if we have multiple active MSAs.
2) Term and termination: add a 30-day cure period for non-payment tied to committed capacity credits, and clarify that capacity top-ups billed in arrears will prorate to the next invoice.
3) SLA and credits: for reserved pools, include an availability target (99.9% monthly) and a defined credit matrix; link to Console-level monitoring metrics for dispute resolution.
4) Data processing: BrightPixel's redline adds a data retention clause in the SOW; propose instead to reference our standard DPA exhibit to keep data obligations centralized.
5) Implementation acceptance: define acceptance as "connector demonstrates connectivity and meets baseline p99 latency <= 120ms and end-to-end throughput >= X rps for two consecutive days" — product to confirm X.

I am attaching: BrightPixel_OrderForm_20250721_annotated.xlsx and BF_SOW_Suggested_Markup.docx. Please review.

Laura — can you confirm whether Finance needs a separate billing annex for blended rates, or if the Order Form table is sufficient? Markus — please check the SLA draft.

Karthik
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference

Attachments: BrightPixel_OrderForm_20250721_annotated.xlsx; BF_SOW_Suggested_Markup.docx

From: Sasha Cohen <sasha.cohen@brightpixel.com>

Subject: Re: BrightPixel — proposed capacity ramp + SOW edits

Thanks Karthik, Vanessa — the changes look reasonable. A few clarifying points from our side: 
- We can reference your DPA if that keeps things simpler.
- For acceptance baseline, we suggest X = 400 rps (this is internal baseline for our ingestion pipeline). Can Redwood confirm whether the implementation team can validate p99 latency <= 120ms at 400 rps?
- For availability credits, BrightPixel requests the SLA table be included in the Order Form itself (procurement asks for a single doc to attach to our PO).

If you can get the finalized redline this week (latest Mon 2025-07-28), we will circulate to our procurement and legal and aim to sign the week of 2025-08-03.

Best,
Sasha
